title: Surrey Village Chef Kaiyum Dewan Khan Named UK's Best at BCA Awards
excerpt: The Spice Lounge head chef took BCA Chef of the Year 2026 at a London gala, after a 55-finalist national cook-off — the Mytchett restaurant's third honour this year.
body:
• Kaiyum Dewan Khan, head chef at Spice Lounge in the Surrey village of Mytchett, has been named BCA Chef of the Year 2026 at the Bangladesh Caterers Association UK Awards.
  • He collected the prize at the BCA's 19th Annual Awards and Gala Dinner on November 1 at the Park Plaza Westminster Bridge Hotel in London, after a national cook-off that drew 55 finalists from hundreds of applicants.
  • Spice Lounge also won Curry Expert of the Year at the English Curry Awards 2026 and was a top-10 regional finalist at the ARTA 2026 awards.
  • To try his cooking: Spice Lounge, Mytchett Road, Camberley GU16 6EG, is open daily 5:30–10:30 p.m. with a banquet night on Thursdays; the chef's recommendation dishes are priced at £10.90.

A chef in a small Surrey village has been named the UK's best in his field. Kaiyum Dewan Khan, who heads the kitchen at Spice Lounge in Mytchett, was named BCA Chef of the Year 2026 at the Bangladesh Caterers Association (BCA) UK Awards, collecting his prize alongside his colleagues at the association's 19th Annual Awards and Gala Dinner on November 1 at the Park Plaza Westminster Bridge Hotel in London.

Won in a cook-off, not on reputation

The BCA title is earned at the stove. The association's Chef of the Year Cook-off 2026, held at Hammersmith & Fulham College in west London, brought together 55 finalists selected from hundreds of applicants across the UK, including 11 women chefs. This year's competition ran under the theme "Honouring Today's Achievements, Inspiring Tomorrow's Success." BCA President Oli Khan MBE described the cook-off as "not merely a competition but a vital platform for the future generation of the culinary arts." The BCA is the main umbrella organisation representing the British-Bangladeshi restaurant and curry industry, and its awards have recognised the sector's chefs and restaurants for nearly two decades.

"We were finalists last year and this year winners, which is brilliant news."

— Mukta Choudhary, manager, Spice Lounge

Spice Lounge manager Mukta Choudhary said the team strives to maintain high standards in the kitchen and front of house, and that the restaurant keeps updating its sauces in response to customer feedback. Customers quoted in local coverage describe the restaurant as a "little gem," praising the food and service.

A kitchen collecting honours

The BCA title is not Spice Lounge's only recognition this year. The restaurant, near Camberley, won Curry Expert of the Year at the English Curry Awards 2026 this summer, and was shortlisted among the top 10 finalists for Regional Restaurant of the Year for Surrey at the Asian Restaurant and Takeaway Awards (ARTA) 2026.

If you go

Spice Lounge sits on Mytchett Road in Mytchett, between Frimley and Ash Vale — full address Mytchett Road, Mytchett, Camberley, GU16 6EG. It is open seven days a week, 5:30–10:30 p.m., with a banquet night every Thursday. The menu runs to traditional dishes — korma, bhuna, dopiaza, tandoori and biryani — plus Chef Khan's recommendations, including chicken or lamb rajastani and chicken jaipuri, each at £10.90. Street parking is available. Bookings: 01252 511181 or online at spiceloungemytchett.co.uk.
